subject: Binning for points with no detections?

messages.author: 9bf7d632f628dfaa
messages.subject: Binning for points with no detections?
parts:
Hi all, 

I have a question about how to include points in which there were no detections when distances are binned. 

I am working with point count data (so, point transects), attempting to estimate bird abundances. The distances are binned, however, because I am doing this species by species, there will be many points in which a given species was not detected. Additionally, there are a number of points in which no birds were detected. I want to include these points in the abundance analysis to get accurate detection probabilities, but I am not sure how to code the 'distbegin' and 'distend' columns for these points. When I attempt to create bins for these data and include points in which a species was not detected, with an NA in the distance column, I get this error:

Error in create.bins(all.data, c(0, 50, 100)) : 
  Some distances are NA, can't create bins.

This seems like a potentially common question with an easy solution, so I apologize if this has been answered previously, but I've been struggling to find an answer

Thanks for any help.
Best,
Sam

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Binning for points with no detections?
parts:
Sam

I've had a look through the source code of the function create.bins  and find that the error message you report was removed from that function this past July 2019 when there were revisions to the Distance package.  I suggest you install a newer version of Distance like this:

remotes::install_github("distancedevelopment/Distance")

and make another attempt to analyse your multi-species data.

Let us know if this works for you; if not, we'll take next steps.

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Binning for points with no detections?
parts:
Sam

Sorry my suggestion did not work.  I've done a bit more thinking and wonder if this works for you.  Treat your distance data (collected as binned) by supplying the midpoint of the distance interval.  Then provide a "cutpoints" argument to the ds() function to have the data binned for analysis.

Here is a silly example I manufactured:

d1 <- rep(0.5,24)
d2 <- rep(1.5,20)
d3 <- rep(2.5,12)
d4 <- rep(3.5,4)
dna <- rep(NA, 10)
dist <- c(d1,d2,d3,d4,dna)
t1 <- rep(1, 24)
t2 <- rep(2,20)
t3 <- rep(3,12)
t4 <- rep(4,4)
tna <- seq(from=5, to=14)
samlab <- c(t1,t2,t3,t4,tna)
area <- 10
eff <- 2
reglab <- "Fred"
mydata <- data.frame(Region.Label=reglab,
                     Area=area,
                     Sample.Label=samlab,
                     Effort=eff,
                     distance=dist)
myresult <- ds(mydata, cutpoints = c(0,1,2,3,4))

Here the entered distances (0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 3.5) are the midpoints of the distance intervals (0,1), (1,2), (2,3), (3,4).  In addition to all the other silliness, I've placed all the detections for bin 1 into transect 1, bin 2 into transect 2,... and no detections in transects 5-14.  But the point is that ds() seems happy enough calling "create.bins" via the use of the "cutpoints" argument.  It is not necessary for you to call "create.bins" yourself.


See if this works for your data.

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Binning for points with no detections?
parts:
Hi Eric,

Great! That seems to work...at least I am able to get results for most species-stratum combinations.

I am still, however, running into some issues/questions about how the Distance incorporates the points in which a species was not detected (but this record needs to be included in the detection probability estimation).

As I have it now, my data input to the ds function includes columns for: Sample.Label (as characters), Region.Label (as factors), Effort (as numeric), Area (as numeric), distance (as integer), size (as integer), and Observer (as a factor). How would you code values for each of these columns for point visits (Sample.Label), in which the species I'm estimating density for was not detected? Currently I leave Sample.Label, Region.Label, Effort, Area, and Observer as the values they should be, but input an NA for both the distance and size columns. Is it a problem that within the distance and size columns I have both numbers and NAs?

I ask, because I am finding that for some species, the model in which I include Observer as a covariate (mod <- ds(mod.data, truncation = 100, transect = "point", key = "hn", formula=~Observer, cutpoints= c(0,50,100))) will not estimate density and shows this error:

Half-normal key function selected.
Model contains covariate term(s): no adjustment terms will be included.
Fitting half-normal key function
AIC= 4
Some variance-covariance matrix elements were NA, possible numerical problems; only estimating detection function.

I thought this had to do with how the points in which the species were not detected are coded, however, some species are able to get estimates from this model, even when they also include points in which the species was not detected.

Any thoughts on this?

Thanks again,
Sam
